title: Escarpment and Wreck
premise: Ulyana Fairweather, a storm chaser drowning in debts owed to the Meridian Syndicate—a crew of dangerous optimists—chases a freak tide along the Cornish escarpment and discovers a sea cave the legends say charges admission: a truth, a price, or a life. Inside, she and her estranged half-brother Caspian, sent by the Syndicate to collect, find a wreck holding her family's stolen inheritance and evidence that the Syndicate's founder caused the original disaster. To bring the expedition home without revealing what it found, Ulyana must choose between loyalty to the people who kept her moving and the truth that could finally let her stop. In the end she trades the wreck's gold for the evidence, pays her debts with the truth itself, and chooses Caspian and the open road over the fortune that would have cost her everything.
about_author: Beatrix Halloran is a former marine cartographer who spent a decade charting coastlines before turning to fiction, and her novels are known for weather that behaves like a character. She lives in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage with an untrustworthy barometer and a dog named Squall.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She outruns a supercell in Oklahoma while dodging calls from the Meridian Syndicate, who financed her last chase and want repayment in 'opportunities.' Establishes her rule: never stop moving. Emotional beat: restless dread beneath bravado.

chapters.title: A Letter with Salt Water Stains
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A solicitor's letter summons her to Cornwall: her estranged mother's estate sits on the escarpment, and the Syndicate 'generously' offers to fund the trip—if she takes their man. Emotional beat: suspicion wrapped in homesickness.

chapters.title: The Man Who Smiled Like Collateral
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. Introduced on the flight over: the Syndicate's collector, charming, meticulous, secretly her half-brother—a fact he knows and she doesn't. His brief: recover the debt or the asset. Emotional beat: duty at war with curiosity.

chapters.title: Escarpment
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. First sight of the crumbling cliff village and the derelict Fairweather cottage, where she finds her mother's storm journals—pages missing, pages redacted. Emotional beat: grief arriving late and sideways.

chapters.title: Legends Charge Admission
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. In the village pub, an old fisherman recounts the cave legend: the sea opens once a generation, and it takes a truth, a price, or a life. Caspian logs it as leverage; Ulyana logs it as weather. Emotional beat: two readers, one text, opposite readings.

chapters.title: Spring Tide, Falling Barometer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Her instruments predict an impossible low tide in three days. The Syndicate calls: they know about the cave too, and they want what's inside. Emotional beat: the trap closing gently, like weather.

chapters.title: What the Mother Hid
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. He finds the hidden half of the journals: their mother documented a 1979 wreck inside the cave and a cargo manifest bearing the Syndicate founder's name. He says nothing. Emotional beat: the first deliberate lie.

chapters.title: Descent at Slack Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The tide retreats; she and Caspian rope down into the revealed cave mouth as the sea waits offshore like a held breath. Emotional beat: exhilaration sharpened by distrust.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian Star
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Inside: a wrecked brig, sealed strongboxes, and a skeleton with the Syndicate founder's signet ring—proof he scuttled his own ship to steal the Fairweather inheritance. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Rising water traps them in a side chamber; to escape they must each sacrifice something—Caspian abandons the Syndicate's recovery equipment, Ulyana leaves her mother's original journal to the sea. Emotional beat: the legend collecting its fee.

chapters.title: Surface
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. They emerge at dawn, alive, changed, and bound by shared secret. Caspian reports a cave, no wreck—his first betrayal of the Syndicate. Emotional beat: loyalty quietly changing sides.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Arrives
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Three Syndicate vessels anchor offshore; the founder's heir, Vespera Meridian, comes ashore with lawyers and divers, certain the cave holds her family's lost fortune. Emotional beat: menace in polite gloves.

chapters.title: Time Is Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. Vespera reveals the storm season's final window: the cave will collapse within two weeks. She gives them until then to 'cooperate.' Emotional beat: a deadline dressed as a courtesy.

chapters.title: Half-Brother
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She discovers Caspian's identity in the solicitor's files—their mother's first family, given up. Confrontation on the cliff edge in rising wind. Emotional beat: betrayal and kinship in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. Ulyana reveals she photographed the manifest and ring before the sea took the originals. They strike an uneasy alliance: use the evidence to break the debt, not enrich either family. Emotional beat: trust built from shared leverage.

chapters.title: Storm Chaser's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She offers Vespera a deal: her silence about the ring in exchange for debt forgiveness. Vespera counters—hand over the photos or Caspian takes the fall for the Syndicate's salvage 'theft.' Emotional beat: love against duty, both directions.

chapters.title: The Night the Sea Came Early
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A rogue storm hits early; Vespera's divers enter the cave against all warning. The escarpment begins to fail. Ulyana must choose: warn the people destroying her family or let the sea collect. Emotional beat: conscience over vengeance.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Collapsing Mouth
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Caspian's POV, interleaved. They go back down in the storm's eye and pull two drowning divers out as the cave mouth crumbles behind them. Vespera watches from the boat. Emotional beat: heroism as its own argument.

chapters.title: What the Cave Kept
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. The collapse exposes the wreck's final hold to the open sea—and to Vespera's cameras. The secret is out; the only currency left is the truth of who caused the wreck. Emotional beat: relief and terror at once.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the village hall, she publishes the manifest and her mother's journal pages: the Syndicate founder murdered the crew and stole the Fairweather inheritance. The village, the solicitor, and the press witness it. Emotional beat: truth as a storm that finally breaks clean.

chapters.title: Payment in Full
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. Vespera, exposed and legally cornered, forgives the debt to buy silence about her family's crime—and Caspian refuses the hush money, choosing Ulyana and the truth. Emotional beat: duty finally kneeling to love.

chapters.title: Escarpment and Wreck
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Weeks later: the debt is dead, the cottage is hers, and the sea has taken the cave for good. She and Caspian load the storm-chasing truck and drive toward the next horizon—stopping, at last, only when they choose. Emotional beat: stillness that costs nothing, for the first time.
